title: Integer Square Root
statement: A tile setter wants the largest square patio that uses at most x unit tiles. Given a non-negative integer x, return the side length of that patio: the largest integer k such that k*k <= x (the floor of the square root of x). Do not use any built-in root function or fractional exponent; x = 0 must return 0 and x = 1 must return 1. The answer space [0, x] is monotonic in the predicate k*k <= x, so binary search it.
hints: The array isn't sorted -- there is no array. What range of candidate answers is monotonic in the check k*k <= x?
Binary search left=0, right=x with while left <= right; if mid*mid <= x the answer is mid or larger (left = mid + 1), otherwise right = mid - 1.
When the loop exits, left has moved one past the last k whose square fits, so return right -- it holds the largest k with k*k <= x (returning left gives floor+1, e.g. 3 for x=8).
